title: Denmark vs Portugal: Ronaldo's Crisis and the Decisive Match
seoTitle: Denmark vs Portugal: Ronaldo's Crisis and Decisive Match
subtitle: What happened between Cristiano Ronaldo and Jorge Jesus and how the match unfolded
excerpt: The Denmark vs Portugal Nations League match made headlines after Cristiano Ronaldo left the training camp amidst a dispute with Jorge Jesus.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The match between Denmark and Portugal, held at Parken Stadium in Copenhagen, was marked by an episode of tension between Cristiano Ronaldo and Jorge Jesus. Portugal's captain left the training camp after an argument with the coach, generating significant buzz among fans.

Ronaldo and the Dispute with Jorge Jesus

During preparations for the second match against Norway, Jorge Jesus promised Ronaldo he would play him in the final minutes but did not deliver. The player stopped training on Tuesday and Wednesday, and, after speaking with the president of the Portuguese Football Federation, decided to leave the training camp.

The Match Itself: 2-2 and Penalties

The match ended in a 2-2 draw. Rasmus Hojlund scored for Denmark, while João Cancelo and Gonçalo Ramos scored for Portugal. The decision went to penalties, where Portugal emerged victorious. The game featured moments of high pressure and Danish counter-attacks.

Squads and Coaches of Each National Team

Portugal featured Diogo Costa, João Cancelo, Rúben Dias, Renato Veiga, Nuno Mendes, Vitinha, Bruno Fernandes, João Neves, João Félix, Pedro Neto, and Gonçalo Ramos, under the leadership of Pedro Neto. Denmark started with Hermansen, Kristensen, Provstgaard, Andersen, Maehle, Hjulmand, Hojbjerg, Damsgaard, Daramy, and Hojlund, led by Brian Riemer.

Broadcast and Schedule

The match was broadcast live by Sportv and also covered in Real Time by ge. The game kicked off at 3:45 PM (Brasília time) on Sunday, October 1, 2026.

Impact on the Nations League Standings

Portugal leads Group A4 with six points after two victories. Denmark remains with three points. A victory in Copenhagen would be decisive for Portugal's advancement to the next phase of the competition.

With information from ge, A Bola.
